description: A procedure body without RETURN yields one NULL row (named after the procedure); DML-only bodies apply their effects; an explicit RETURN still wins. Converted 1:1 from procedures/ProcedureImplicitNullReturnTest and jdbc/CallReturnlessProcedureJdbcTest (both now retired — the JDBC variant duplicated the same SQL semantics through the driver).

steps.sql:
CREATE PROCEDURE mark_ids(ids ARRAY)
RETURNS STRING
LANGUAGE SQL
AS
$$
BEGIN
    MERGE INTO del_marks AS target
        USING (SELECT CAST(VALUE AS TEXT) AS id FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(input => :ids))) AS source
        ON target.id = source.id
        WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id) VALUES (source.id);
EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHER THEN
        RETURN 'error';
END;
$$

CREATE PROCEDURE mark(ids ARRAY)
RETURNS STRING
LANGUAGE SQL
AS
$$
BEGIN
    MERGE INTO marks AS target
        USING (SELECT CAST(VALUE AS TEXT) AS id FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(input => :ids))) AS source
        ON target.id = source.id
        WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id) VALUES (source.id);
EXCEPTION
    WHEN OTHER THEN
        RETURN 'error';
END;
$$
